h1: Sumali Villa Sing Buri — a garden pool villa where the owners welcome you in person
intro: If you want a Sing Buri stay that isn't a tower hotel but a quiet villa home with a pool in the garden, where the owner steps out to greet you at check-in — Sumali Villa is a tiny boutique villa of just 4 rooms inside the architect-designed home of a Thai-French couple in Tambon Chaksi, near Wat Phra Non Chaksi · it's a popular overnight stop for drivers heading north from Bangkok who'd rather sleep in a garden-home mood than a roadside hotel · rooms start at around THB 1,200/night · it scores about 8.4 from real guest reviews, with the pool, gardens and owners' hospitality singled out most.

body.html: What sets Sumali Villa apart from other Sing Buri stays is that it's a genuine architect's home, not a hotel built to sell rooms · the 540 sqm house was designed by the owners — a Thai-French couple — who turned the upper floor into just 4 guest rooms · walk in and you meet an outdoor pool and a beautifully tended garden, the first thing nearly every real review mentions · the feeling is less like checking into a hotel and more like staying at the home of a friend with good taste.

Get the location straight first · the villa sits in Tambon Chaksi, Mueang Sing Buri, about 2 km from the town centre, near Wat Phra Non Chaksi Worawihan, one of the province's important temples · it's roughly a 5-minute drive to town and the markets and about 20 minutes to the Bang Rachan camp memorial · the upside is the quiet, garden mood, but the trade-off is that there's nothing within walking distance — you need a car · several reviews note that the entrance signage and reception point aren't obvious, so first-timers can get a little lost — open your map app and call the owners ahead.

The four rooms are named after flowers — Lupin, Lys, Laurier, Rose — each 25 sqm and up, with a private balcony, a lounge sofa corner, a flat-screen TV, minibar, coffee maker and en-suite bathroom · real reviews praise the roomy spaces, comfortable beds and good showers · cleanliness, comfort and the staff/owners all score above 8.5 on the platforms · Wi-Fi gets mixed notes — some call it very good, others say the signal is weak in spots, so set expectations if you need to work online seriously.

"It felt like staying at a friend's house — the owner came out to welcome us, the pool was lovely, the garden shady, the room clean, and breakfast was the best of the whole trip. A genuinely relaxing stop on the way north."

Let's be honest that the "it's really the owners' home" side has both upsides and things to know · the upside is the warm, attentive welcome — the owners recommend places to eat and visit and look after you themselves · but guests share the common areas like the pool and garden with the owners, their family and their friends · some reviews therefore feel privacy is more limited than at a hotel, and a couple of rooms have bathrooms that aren't fully partitioned · if you want total, see-nobody privacy, weigh this up.

Another point reviews raise is the breakfast, which costs around 270 baht per person extra · many call it tasty and freshly made, but some feel the price is steep for an out-of-town location and that the choice isn't very wide · in-room items are occasionally short of what's expected, such as robes or slippers, and a few reviews mention small day-to-day upkeep niggles · overall these are minor things to be aware of, not deal-breakers.

Overall, Sumali Villa scores about 8.4 out of 10 across real guest reviews on several platforms and ranks among Sing Buri's top villa-style stays · it isn't a hotel with every facility, and it isn't for people who want to walk around a town centre · but measured as a quiet villa home with a garden pool, owners who host in person, a praised breakfast, and prices starting around THB 1,200 and rising to about THB 1,500 by room and season — it does the job of a relaxing overnight stop on the way north, or an easy Sing Buri getaway, very well, as long as you have a car and can accept sharing the common areas.

honestSummary: Sumali Villa is the right pick if you want to overnight in a quiet villa home with a garden pool, where the owners welcome you in person — a garden mood, a praised breakfast, near Wat Phra Non Chaksi · the trade-offs are a location that needs a car, sharing the common areas with the owners, and a breakfast charged at around 270 baht per person.
honestChecks: If you want total, see-nobody privacy — this is genuinely the owners' home and guests share the pool and garden with the family → if that matters to you, look at an in-town Sing Buri hotel instead.

If you don't have your own car — the villa is out of town in Tambon Chaksi with nothing in walking distance → if you'd rather stroll the riverfront in town, look at Chaisaeng Palace on the Chao Phraya instead.

If you plan to eat breakfast here — it's charged at around 270 baht per person, which some find steep for an out-of-town spot → if you're not fussed, drive into town for cheaper morning options near the market.

faq.q: Where is Sumali Villa in Sing Buri, and what's nearby?
faq.a: The villa is at 29 Moo 1, Tambon Chaksi, Mueang Sing Buri, about 2 km from the town centre · it's near Wat Phra Non Chaksi Worawihan · roughly a 5-minute drive to town and the markets and about 7 minutes to the Chao Phraya riverfront · the Bang Rachan memorial and Wat Phikun Thong are 20-25 minutes further · nothing is within walking distance, so you need a car.

faq.q: How much does Sumali Villa cost, and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rooms start at around THB 1,200/night · there are just 4 rooms named after flowers — Lys, Laurier, Rose, and the larger Lupin that sleeps more · each is 25 sqm and up with a private balcony and lounge corner · prices rise by room and season to about THB 1,500, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Sumali Villa have a pool, and what's it like?
faq.a: Yes · there's an outdoor pool set in a well-tended garden, the feature real reviews praise most, plus a small fitness corner and free parking · because it's genuinely the owners' home, guests share the pool and garden with the owners and their family.

faq.q: What's breakfast like at Sumali Villa, and is it included?
faq.a: Breakfast is charged at around 270 baht per person and isn't included in the room rate · many reviews praise it as freshly made and tasty — some call it the best of their trip — but a few feel the price is steep for an out-of-town location and that the choice isn't very wide.

faq.q: Who is Sumali Villa best for?
faq.a: It suits drivers who want to overnight in a quiet villa home with a garden pool, and couples after a garden-home mood · you get a warm welcome from the Thai-French owners, a praised breakfast, and a spot near Wat Phra Non Chaksi · but you need a car since it's out of town, and you must be comfortable sharing the common areas with the owners.

faq.q: Is Sumali Villa hard to find?
faq.a: Be ready for it · the entrance signage and reception point aren't obvious, and many reviews say it's confusing first time, with a short walk from parking to the house · open your map app and call the owners ahead — it's a small villa, so they can guide you in and come out to meet you.
